briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for November 9, 2026.

sections.title: 🌍 COP31 Opens: A Crucial Test for Climate Action
sections.content: The 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) has opened in Türkiye today. Australia is leading the negotiations, and with the Paris Agreement's 1.5-degree target at risk, the issue of AI power consumption is expected to be the first agenda item [5, 18]. Marking 10 years since the Paris Agreement, the focus of climate response is shifting from setting targets to actual implementation, with discussions on climate finance and greenhouse gas reduction gaining attention [6, 19, 75]. However, concerns have been raised that low participation from heads of state has put climate politics in a more precarious situation than the climate crisis itself, and there are predictions that it will be a testbed for climate action amid the energy crisis [7, 11].

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and the Suffering of Vulnerable Nations
sections.content: Nepal, responsible for only 0.01% of carbon emissions, suffered 6 trillion won in damages from severe floods, highlighting the issue of climate crisis responsibility with the opening of COP31 [1, 4]. This demonstrates that the climate crisis is not a future problem but an ongoing phenomenon, with low-contributing nations like Bhutan bearing immense costs [99, 100]. Furthermore, health threats are intensifying due to climate change, with the spread of 'superbugs' and warnings about antibiotic ineffectiveness [20]. Damages in the agricultural sector are becoming a reality, with fruit trees in Syria and banana producers in Latin America struggling due to drought and climate change, demanding wage increases [90, 92].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Achievements
sections.content: Domestically, Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) has repeatedly received the Minister of Climate's Commendation at the '2026 Korea Carbon Neutrality and Green Management Awards' for reducing its own greenhouse gas emissions by 36.2% [2, 9, 12, 21, 23, 36, 46]. Korea Midland Power (KOMIPO) also demonstrated its carbon neutrality achievements by transitioning its thermal power-centric business structure and contributing to greenhouse gas reduction, earning a Presidential Commendation [10, 32, 34, 38, 42, 48, 51]. The APEC Climate Center (APCC) has also made international contributions by supporting Peru's agricultural response to the climate crisis, establishing local climate information utilization systems, and promoting technical cooperation [3, 8]. Various local governments are also spreading a culture of carbon neutrality practice by hosting citizen participation workshops for carbon neutrality [28, 31, 33], organizing eco-friendly festivals [30, 44], and establishing resource circulation systems [40, 45, 49, 50].

sections.title: ⚡ Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Challenges Ahead
sections.content: The International Energy Agency (IEA) analyzed that the energy security crisis has fueled the explosive growth of renewable energy [67], and following the Democratic Party's landslide victory, the 'Blue Tsunami' in the U.S., renewable energy-related stocks are gaining attention, indicating an accelerating transition to renewable energy [73]. Microsoft's (MS) purchase of 40 GW of renewable energy, viewing clean power acquisition as a key to AI competitiveness, suggests that renewable energy is a core driver for future industries [62]. Domestically, KEPCO KDN is accelerating solar power projects utilizing public idle land, and Ulsan City is forming an offshore wind power council, demonstrating a full-fledged effort to foster renewable energy [66, 71, 74]. However, cases like Germany's expansion of gas power after phasing out nuclear energy [41, 64] and the paradox of high electricity prices in Spain despite increased renewable energy [59] illustrate the complex challenges in the energy transition process, also raising the need for improved risk management systems [60, 63].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing. This is a time when our efforts for a sustainable future become even more crucial.
